# Full-parity witness forests

This note records exact consequences of the finite certificate in
`candidate d2b290ebd8e35052`. These consequences do not by
themselves prove a depth lower bound.

Let P=pi(C) intersect Z^n. Suppose a polyhedron

    L = {z : a_i.z <= beta_i, 1<=i<=s}

has int(L) intersect P empty, and has witnesses p_i in P such that

    a_i.p_i=beta_i,     a_j.p_i<beta_j for every j!=i.

All retained normals are nonzero, and L is full-dimensional. The original
cap-circuit certificate also has h_i<beta_i, positive continuous-normal
circuits whose integer sum is a_i.z-h_i, and constituent cap masses <T.
Those additional mass and contact conditions are not used until the basin
cover conclusion below.

## 1. The witness convex hull is empty, including its relative boundary

Every convex combination of at least two distinct witnesses strictly
satisfies every inequality of L: for inequality i, at most its own witness
can have equality, and at least one other witness occurs with positive
coefficient. Such a combination belongs to int(L).

Every integer point in W=conv{p_i} belongs to P, since W is contained in
pi(C). It follows that

    W intersect Z^n = {p_1,...,p_s}.

Moreover each p_i is a vertex of W, since its own linear functional strictly
separates it from every other witness. This argument does not require W to
have dimension n. It excludes extra integer points on relative faces as well
as in the relative interior.

As usual, midpoint parity then proves s<=m=2^n. Assume henceforth that s=m.
There is exactly one witness p_r in every residue class r modulo 2.

## 2. A deterministic map, with exact preimages

For z in Z^n define

    R(z) = (z+p_[z mod 2])/2.

This is an integer point. Its complete inverse image at any y in Z^n is

    R^{-1}(y) = {2y-p_r : r in (Z/2Z)^n}.

The m displayed points are distinct and have the required parity r. Thus
every target has exactly m preimages in the full lattice and at most m
preimages in P. Each witness is fixed by R. Convexity gives R(P) subset P.

Every orbit in the entire integer lattice terminates at a witness. Indeed,
an orbit starting at z remains in the bounded convex hull of {z} and W, so
it is eventually periodic. If a cycle has period k and successive digits
p_0,...,p_{k-1}, iterating the defining identity gives

    (2^k-1) z_0 = sum_(j=0)^(k-1) 2^j p_j.

Hence z_0 lies in W and is an integer, so it is a witness vertex. All weights
in this convex combination are positive. Extremality of that witness forces
all digits to equal it; thus the cycle is a fixed point.

## 3. Exact orbit coefficients and basin geometry

Write z_0=z, z_{j+1}=R(z_j), p_j=p_[z_j mod 2], and suppose z_k=p_s is the
terminal witness. Then

    2^k p_s = z + sum_(j=0)^(k-1) 2^j p_j,

or equivalently

    z-p_s = sum_(j=0)^(k-1) 2^j (p_s-p_j).

Define m_r=sum_{j:p_j=p_r}2^j for r!=s. The identity becomes

    z = (1+sum_(r!=s) m_r) p_s - sum_(r!=s) m_r p_r.

All m_r are nonnegative integers. Thus a basin is contained in the integer
semigroup generated by the outward edge vectors p_s-p_r. For z!=p_s,
at least one coefficient with r!=s is positive; otherwise the displayed
identity would give z=p_s. Strict supporting inequalities imply

    a_s.z > beta_s                  for z!=p_s in basin s.

At the root itself there is equality. Therefore L intersect P consists
exactly of the witnesses. This conclusion is stronger than interior-freeness.

In the cap certificate, beta_s>h_s. Consequently a_s.z>h_s on the ENTIRE
basin s, including its root. The open constituent caps of circuit s cover
the entire continuous fiber space above every point of that basin. This is
an exact relation between the deterministic forest and the original caps.
It supplies the elementary bound

    mu(basin s) <= sum_j mu(H_sj) < k_s T <= (d+1) T.

A sharper gamma_d factor does not follow from this covering statement alone.

For another useful potential put V(z)=max_i(a_i.z-beta_i). On P, V>=0,
and V vanishes precisely at the roots. Since each digit belongs to L,

    V(R(z)) <= V(z)/2.

Thus on any fixed finite P, if delta is the smallest positive value of V,
a nonroot orbit can have length at most 1+ceil(log_2(V(z)/delta)).
This is only a bound with geometric parameters, not a dimension-only bound.

## 4. Exact fiber inclusions and volume-root inequalities

Write K_z=C_z. Repeated convexity gives the Minkowski inclusion

    2^{-k} K_z + sum_(j=0)^(k-1) 2^{j-k} K_(p_j) subset K_(p_s).

The coefficients sum to one, and their integer-coordinate barycenter is
p_s by the orbit identity. For d>=1 let f(z)=vol_d(K_z)^{1/d}. The ordinary
Brunn-Minkowski inequality, including zero-volume fibers, gives

    f(z) + sum_(j=0)^(k-1) 2^j f(p_j) <= 2^k f(p_s),

or

    f(z) <= (1+sum_(r!=s)m_r)f(p_s) - sum_(r!=s)m_r f(p_r).

In particular, if all witness fibers have the same volume v_0, every fiber
has volume at most v_0. This includes v_0=0, in which case all fibers have
zero d-volume. The assertion is about volume, not halfspace depth.

If v_0>0 and a source fiber also has volume v_0, equality holds throughout
the iterated Brunn-Minkowski argument. Every positive-volume witness fiber
occurring in that orbit is then homothetic to the source fiber, and equality
of their volumes makes them translates. The intermediate fibers on the
orbit likewise have volume v_0 and are the corresponding Minkowski means.
Here the ordinary equality case of Brunn-Minkowski for convex bodies is
being used; all relevant fibers have full dimension because v_0>0.

## 5. A precise limitation of scalar source budgets

For any nonnegative weights w_z on P, the one-step inequality only yields

    2 sum_z w_z f(Rz) >= sum_z w_z f(z)
                              + sum_z w_z f(p_[z mod 2]).

Reindexing the first term introduces the total weights of the at most m
preimages. Neither the indegree bound nor the signed orbit coefficients
control the total source volume by a dimension-only multiple of the witness
volume.

For example, take C=[0,L]^n x K with L a positive integer and K any
positive-volume convex body. Use roots {0,1}^n. The expanded polyhedron

    sum_(i=1)^n |z_i-1/2| <= n/2

has 2^n facets, and each cube vertex is the unique witness on its own facet
and strictly satisfies all others. Its only integer points are the roots.
All fibers of C have the same volume, and R is coordinatewise ceil(z_i/2).
Every scalar Brunn-Minkowski inequality above is equality, while the total
source volume is (L+1)^n times one witness volume and is arbitrarily large.

This example does not meet the missing strict SMALL-cap requirements for
roots placed there when the target T is below the OC value. It proves only
that the graph, geometric witnesses, contraction, and scalar volume-root
inequalities alone cannot imply that a root is deep or supply a bounded
source budget. Any successful use of this forest must retain the original
cap masses and their cross-circuit contact conditions.

## 6. An exact telescoping slack identity

Let

    g(z)=2f(Rz)-f(z)-f(p_[z mod 2]) >= 0.

This is the complete one-step Brunn-Minkowski slack, including any extra
volume between the Minkowski mean and the containing original fiber. Along
a terminating orbit as above, simple substitution gives the EXACT identity

    f(z) = 2^k f(p_s) - sum_(j=0)^(k-1) 2^j f(p_j)
                          - sum_(j=0)^(k-1) 2^j g(z_j).

In the equal-witness case it reads

    f(z) = f_0 - sum_(j=0)^(k-1) 2^j g(z_j).

Consequently the sum of amplified slacks along any orbit is at most f_0.
For arbitrary nonnegative source weights w_z this can be summed exactly:

    sum_z w_z f(z) + sum_t A_w(t) g(t) = sum_r C_w(r) f(p_r),

where A_w(t) sums 2^j w_z over all visits z_j=t before termination, and
C_w(r) is the sum of the signed orbit coefficients at root r. The A_w are
nonnegative, but the C_w need not be. They satisfy

    sum_r C_w(r) = sum_z w_z,
    sum_r C_w(r) p_r = sum_z w_z z.

Thus a positive-root-budget interpretation requires an additional argument
for the signs and sizes of C_w. Already for roots 0,1 and P={0,...,L}, with
unit weights, C_w(0)=(L+1)(1-L/2) is negative for L>2, while
C_w(1)=L(L+1)/2. This rules out silently interpreting the telescoping identity
as a convex transport of source volume into bounded witness budgets.
